label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, C, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a closed cylinder with a rolled rim at the top and at the bottom, which is what a 55-gallon drum is. In FRONT, LEFT, BACK and RIGHT the sides are straight and the ends square. The TOP and BELOW views show a round lid and base with a bevelled edge. Nothing sticks out wrongly; the only protrusion is the small knob on the side wall, which is a detail rather than an outline fault.

M2.reason: Measured 24.4 x 24 x 36 units against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: the height is 5.9% over and the width 6.1% over, both within the 15% band for a brief size (sizeOff 0.061).

M3.reason: The brief asks for a drum body, rust and a hazard stripe. All three are there: the body is a closed cylinder, the stripe runs round its middle (front, left, back, right views), and the rust is on the top and bottom rims. The top and bottom rims are also present, and the rim outline is faceted in the top view, which is fine for a round part. The bung is an extra small part the brief does not ask for.

M4.reason: The rims are rust brown, and the hazard stripe is yellow and black, both as the brief asks. The body is a blue-grey painted steel with mottling, and it reads as weathered paint rather than the rusted steel the brief names (rust appears only on the rims; the body has no brown or orange rust patches). That is the same colour family but not the material the brief asks for.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is sharp and in place on all four sides, and the rim rust is clear. The body's wear is soft and blotchy and shows little rust. A vertical texture seam runs down the middle of the FRONT view across both the body and the stripe, where the texture meets itself, and it is visible in FRONT and FRONT-LEFT. Those are detail faults, not shape faults.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the measured line-up. The judges were asked four times which of the four was not made by Valve (the asset at D, A, C, C) and picked C, C, B, D: none picked the asset as the odd one out, so it passed for one of the game's (Half-Life's own at the same scale).

M7.reason: The drum stands upright on its bottom rim, and its base sits at the origin. The brief names no front, and the bung on the side is placed on one face, so the facing is consistent.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks report no errors. Nothing is open or inside out in the views: the top and base are closed discs, and the sides are closed. Triangles are 344. That is past twice the median of Half-Life's props of this size (99, so 198) and past the third quartile (156), but under the most Valve spends on a prop of this size (422), which is the bound the later amendment sets for an original prop. It passes.
